Which specialist insurers actually cover elective cosmetic, dental or bariatric complications abroad?

Standard travel and domestic health policies typically exclude elective surgery abroad and its downstream complications, as highlighted by the [CDC Yellow Book guidance on medical tourism](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html). Instead, travelers generally examine two distinct categories of specialist coverage: international medical-travel policies issued from their home market and local Turkish complication policies issued inside Türkiye.

Examples of international specialist programs include [Medical Travel Shield](https://www.medicaltravelshield.com/cosmetic-surgery) (for UK, EU, and select international residents covering cosmetic, dental, and elective surgery complications) and [Global Protective Solutions / Custom Assurance Placements](https://www.globalprotectivesolutions.com/enroll/) (for US and international medical travelers). Inside Türkiye, local insurers such as [Demir Sağlık](https://healthtourism.demirsaglik.com.tr/Home/Eng) and [Sompo Sigorta](https://www.somposigorta.com.tr/en/complication-insurance) offer Turkish-regulated complication policies—typically covering repeat intervention performed inside Türkiye within a defined window (often 6 months), rather than medical bills back home.

body.text: What exclusions (unlicensed clinics, pre-existing conditions, aesthetic dissatisfaction) apply?

Reading the exclusions schedule matters more than reading the headline benefit limit. Almost every specialist complication policy voids coverage immediately if the procedure takes place at an unlicensed facility or by an unqualified practitioner—making a [Ministry of Health authorized facility check](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) essential before you buy.

Common exclusions also include undisclosed pre-existing medical conditions, smoking or non-compliance with post-operative instructions, experimental or unlisted procedures, and aesthetic dissatisfaction. If a nose, veneer shade, or contour heals safely without infection or clinical failure—even if you dislike the cosmetic look—complication insurance will not fund a revision. Bariatric travelers should also check BMI thresholds and whether multi-procedure combinations (such as tummy tuck plus liposuction plus breast surgery) require higher risk tiers.
What minimum repatriation and extended-hotel limits should you choose?

Emergency medical evacuation and post-operative flight delays are where uninsured costs escalate fastest. As the [CDC Yellow Book](https://www.cdc.gov/yellow-book/hcp/health-care-abroad/medical-tourism.html) notes, flying too soon after surgery raises the risk of deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, meaning a treating doctor may legally prohibit you from boarding your scheduled return flight.

When evaluating policy wording with a licensed broker, look closely at two numbers: the medical and emergency repatriation cap (many specialist policies, such as [Medical Travel Shield's dental and surgical plans](https://www.medicaltravelshield.com/dental-treatment), structure medical and repatriation limits up to £2 million or equivalent high-tier caps to absorb air-ambulance costs) and the extended-stay sub-limit (daily hotel allowance, companion accommodation, and return flight rebooking fees if you are declared unfit to fly for 7 to 14 extra days).
When must the policy be purchased before departure?

Specialist international medical-travel policies must almost always be purchased before you depart your home country—and many require enrollment a set number of days before surgery or within a fixed window after paying your first trip deposit if you want trip-cancellation benefits included. Local Turkish complication policies likewise must be issued before the primary procedure begins; you cannot buy complication cover once an infection or bleeding event has already started.

Verify that your chosen Turkish hospital meets the insurer's licensing and accreditation definition.
Check whether complications are covered only inside Türkiye or also for emergency stabilization and repatriation home.
Review daily caps for extended hotel nights, companion lodging, and new return airfare.
Confirm the exact claim notification hotline (24/7 English assistance) and required discharge paperwork.

faq.q: Does my credit card travel insurance cover surgery complications in Türkiye?
faq.a: Almost never. Credit card and standard annual travel policies exclude planned elective medical, cosmetic, and dental travel and any complications resulting from those procedures.

faq.q: If my Turkish clinic includes "complication insurance" in its package, is that enough?
faq.a: Review the actual policy certificate carefully. Clinic-bundled Turkish policies typically cover repeat clinical intervention inside Türkiye for a limited period, not emergency care or repatriation back to your home country.

faq.q: Does medical complication insurance cover me if I simply dislike my cosmetic result?
faq.a: No. Complication policies cover objective clinical complications such as infection, bleeding, wound dehiscence, or blood clots—never subjective aesthetic dissatisfaction.

faq.q: Can I buy complication insurance after I arrive in Istanbul?
faq.a: International specialist medical-travel policies generally require purchase before departing your home country, while Turkish local policies must be issued before your procedure starts.

faq.q: What happens if my doctor says I am unfit to fly home on my booked date?
faq.a: If your policy includes extended-stay benefits, it may reimburse hotel nights and flight-change fees up to the stated daily and total sub-limits—provided you submit written physician certification.
